previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening skin pain due to calciphylaxis, with concern for superimposed soft tissue infection. She presented with increased pain in wounds on her left hip, right breast, and abdomen after dialysis. Initial labs showed elevated WBC, and she was started on IV clindamycin and ciprofloxacin, later transitioned to oral therapy. Dermatology recommended intralesional sodium thiosulfate injections for outpatient management. The nephrology team increased cinacalcet to 60 mg BID to address elevated PTH contributing to calciphylaxis. The patient reported improved pain control with oxycodone and was willing to pursue injection therapy. She was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a 7-day antibiotic course, continue dialysis, and arrange follow-up with dermatology and surgery. Concerns about her current dialysis center were documented for care coordination.

c/b calciphylaxis, CAD s/p CABG who initially presented to the 
ED from dialysis when she had a single episode of hematemesis. 
GI was consulted and did not recommend EGD at this time as H&H 
stable and there was no further evidence of bleeding. The 
patient did not receive any PRBCs. She continued to have stable 
H/H and did not have further episodes. During her hospital stay, 
she complained of severe nausea and pain from calciphylaxis 
lesions, and initially could not tolerate PO. Sodium thiosulfate 
was stopped, and nausea greatly improved with increased PO 
intake. She was followed by Palliative Care and her pain regimen 
was increased.

==============
ACUTE ISSUES
==============
#Hematemasis due to ___ Tear: Patient experienced 
coffee ground emesis after dialysis on day of presentation. She 
reports that she normally has emesis post-dialysis but has never 
had this bleeding before. She likely had a small ___ 
tear ___ vomiting. Cannot rule out other common caused of upper 
GI bleed, such as ulcers, gastritis, AVMs. In ED, had NGT placed 
with return of minimal coffee ground fluid. GI saw patient in ED 
decided against scope given clinical stability. Throughout her 
hospital stay she had no further episodes of bleeding, her H/H 
was stable.   

#Nausea due to medication adverse effect: Pt reported 
significant nausea making it difficult to tolerate food or PO 
medications. This was thought to be due to sodium thiosulfate as 
it is a known adverse effect of this medication. It was stopped, 
and her nausea improved, and her food intake improved 
signficantly. However, she still refused to take most of her PO 
medications throughout her inpatient stay due to fears of 
nausea. She best tolerated pills when they were crushed and 
given with ice cream. She was initially treated with standing IV 
ondansetron, but this was changed to PRN prior to discharge and 
pt did not require it. She was followed by nutrition. 

#Calciphylaxis: Pt had significant pain due to multiple 
calciphylaxis lesions. She was followed by Palliative Care with 
uptitration of her pain regimen. A goals of care discussion was 
held with discussion of calciphylaxis. Pt confirms she has a 
good quality of life and wants to continue with hemodialysis at 
this time. Initially she could not tolerate PO medications, but 
ultimately as her nausea improved she was able to transition to 
PO dilaudid crushed and served in ice cream. Final regimen: 
fentanyl 75 mcg q72hr, PO dilaudid ___ q2h:prn pain, with PO 
dilaudid 8mg to be given prior to dressing changes. 

# Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis: Pt initially had anion gap 
metabolic acidosis. Urine and serum tox were negative. This was 
ultimately thought to be due to sodium thiosulfate treatment and 
resolved after cessation of this medication. 

# Leukocytosis: Pt presented with leukocytosis of uncertain 
etiology. Blood and urine cultures were negative. Concern was 
for possible breast abscess, so she was briefly treated with 
vancomycin, but ultrasound did not demonstrate a fluid 
collection. Patient also had multiple skin wounds from 
calciphylaxis, however none of these were concerning for 
infection. A right thigh wound was cultured and grew multiple 
bacteria including pseudomonas, however given her clinical 
stability and lack of concern for infection, these were 
considered to be colonizers and she was not treated with 
antibiotics. 

#Diarrhea: Pt had episode of loose stools after a week in the 
hospital. C. Diff was sent and was negative. Diarrhea resolved.

===============

EXAMINATION:  LEFT BREAST ULTRASOUND

INDICATION:  ___ woman presenting with cellulitis versus abscess of
the left breast.

COMPARISON:  Mammogram from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Left breast ultrasound was performed.

FINDINGS: 

A bedside ultrasound was performed and static and cine images were provided
for interpretation. On these limited images, in the area of clinical concern
in the central outer and central lower left breast, normal appearing breast
tissue is identified.  No drainable collection is noted.

IMPRESSION: 

No drainable collection is identified on this limited portable ultrasound.

RECOMMENDATION:  Repeat formal ultrasound in the Breast Imaging Department is
recommended when feasible.

BI-RADS:  1 Negative.

EXAMINATION:  PORTABLE ABDOMEN

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with ___ year old woman with CAD s/p CABG, HTN,
DM2, asthma, ESRD with leukocytosis and persistent nausea and vomiting  //
please evaluate for obstruction

TECHNIQUE:  Portable radiographs of the abdomen

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

The bowel gas pattern is nonspecific and nonobstructive with no abnormally
dilated loops of large or small bowel. Assessment for free intraperitoneal air
is limited on supine radiographs. If there is significant clinical concern for
pneumoperitoneum, upright and left lateral decubitus radiographs or
cross-sectional imaging should be performed. Osseous structures are
unremarkable. Calcified uterine fibroids and median sternotomy wires are
noted.

IMPRESSION: 

Nonspecific bowel gas pattern with no evidence of obstruction.
